subjectSummary.answer: AMD designs and sells processors, graphics chips, AI accelerators, and related products for data centers, personal computers, gaming, and embedded systems. Its latest supplied quarterly filing reports revenue growth led by data-center products for the six months ended June 27, 2026.

recentMaterialEvents.claim: AMD and Meta announced an expanded partnership on October 27, 2026, covering AI systems, processors, GPUs, networking, and software. AMD said Helios systems are running at Meta and that EPYC processors power Meta's Muse AI agent.
AMD agreed to acquire World Labs for about $8.2 billion in stock. The deal was announced in September 2026 and is subject to regulatory approval and customary closing conditions.
AMD announced that it plans to report fiscal Q3 2026 results on November 3, 2026, after market close.

factLedger.claim: AMD reported total revenue of $21.789 billion for the six months ended June 27, 2026.
For the six months ended June 27, 2026, Data Center revenue was $12.493 billion, Client and Gaming revenue was $7.446 billion, and Embedded revenue was $1.850 billion.
AMD reported 2025 revenue of $16.635 billion for Data Center, $14.550 billion for Client and Gaming, and $3.454 billion for Embedded.
AMD completed the ZT Systems acquisition in March 2025 for $3.2 billion in cash and 8.3 million shares.
AMD's World Labs acquisition agreement was for about $8.2 billion in common shares; the share count was not known when the September 2026 filing was made.

whatItDoes.answer: AMD sells server CPUs, GPUs and AI accelerators; processors and graphics products for computers and gaming; and chips for embedded systems. It also sells or licenses some of its intellectual property.

howItMakesMoney.answer: For the six months ended June 27, 2026, AMD reported revenue of $12.493 billion from Data Center, $7.446 billion from Client and Gaming, and $1.850 billion from Embedded. The filing does not provide revenue shares for these segments in the supplied text.

customers.answer: AMD sells to customers in data centers, computer and gaming markets, and embedded-product markets. No customer made up at least 10% of total revenue in fiscal years 2025 or 2024; one Client and Gaming customer made up 18% in 2023.

geography.answer: The supplied filing text does not give revenue amounts or percentages by region. The 10-K says international sales are expected to remain a significant part of total sales.

companyKpis.answer: For the six months ended June 27, 2026, Data Center revenue was $12.493 billion, Client and Gaming revenue was $7.446 billion, Embedded revenue was $1.850 billion, and total revenue was $21.789 billion. Data Center revenue rose 81% from the same period a year earlier, driven mainly by EPYC processors and Instinct MI350 Series GPUs.

The 10-Q also says results can vary by quarter and season.

sources.title: AMD to Acquire World Labs to Advance the Future of AI Compute :: Advanced Micro Devices, Inc. (AMD)
sources.summary: AMD to Acquire World Labs in a $8.2B all-stock deal to boost AI compute and open ecosystem - What: AMD announces a definitive agreement to acquire World Labs, a San Francisco–based AI model research lab led by Dr. Fei-Fei Li. - Why: Bringing World Labs’ AI model research, spatial-intelligence, 3D environment generation, and robotic learning capabilities to AMD to better align hardware, software, and systems with evolving AI workloads and to strengthen the open AI ecosystem. - Leadership: Fei-Fei Li will join AMD as executive vice president and chief scientist, reporting to CEO Lisa Su. - Scope: The acquisition aims to inform AMD’s future AI infrastructure roadmaps and product strategy, addressing increasingly diverse AI workloads (reasoning, robotics, simulation, physical AI). - Terms and timing: All-stock transaction valued at approximately $8.2 billion, expected to close by end of 2026, subject to regulatory approvals and customary closing conditions. - Impact: Enhances AMD’s AI model research capabilities and accelerates development of AI hardware and software aligned with emerging models and applications.
sources.snippet: AMD to Acquire World Labs to Advance the Future of AI Compute :: Advanced Micro Devices, Inc. (AMD) # AMD to Acquire World Labs to Advance the Future of AI Compute September 28, 2026 4:05 pm EDT Download as PDF ### Acquisition brings leading AI model research expertise to AMD, helping to shape future AI infrastructure and strengthen the open AI ecosystem SANTA CLARA, Calif., Sept. 28, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- AMD (NASDAQ: AMD) today announced that it has entered into a definitive agreement to acquire World Labs, an AI model and research lab led by AI pioneer Dr. Fei-Fei Li. The acquisition will bring a world-class team of researchers and model experts to AMD, strengthening its ability to develop AI hardware, software and systems around the needs of emerging models and applications. As AI expands into reasoning, robotics, simulation and physical AI, the demands on compute infrastructure become more diverse. World Labs’ expertise in developing advanced models will give AMD deeper insight into how workloads are evolving and help shape its future technology roadmaps. The acquisition advances AMD’s strategy to deliver AI infrastructure for an open ecosystem. ...

sources.title: AMD and Meta Advance Strategic Partnership to Power Meta’s Superintelligence Infrastructure :: Advanced Micro Devices, Inc. (AMD)
sources.summary: Summary: AMD and Meta have expanded a strategic partnership to power Meta’s superintelligence infrastructure. Key points: - AMD Helios rackscale solutions are running at Meta and being tested for broader deployment. - AMD EPYC processors support Meta’s Muse AI agent, with Meta as a lead customer for 6th Gen EPYC CPUs; future generations (including Verano) are in development. - AMD Instinct GPUs are used in Meta’s production AI workloads (training, ranking, recommendations); Meta is an early customer for the MI450 architecture and will deploy a custom MI GPU optimized for its workloads; plans include MI500-series GPUs and next-gen rack-scale systems. - Software collaboration includes ROCm with PyTorch, Day-0 support for Meta models (Muse Spark Open on Instinct GPUs; Muse Glimmer on Ryzen AI PCs and Radeon GPUs), and ongoing optimization of large-scale AI training (e.g., recommendation models) on Instinct MI350X GPUs. - Both companies align silicon, software, and systems roadmaps to support Meta’s billions-of-people AI infrastructure at gigawatt scale. - AMD will invest $1 billion in Meta equity.
sources.snippet: AMD and Meta Advance Strategic Partnership to Power Meta’s Superintelligence Infrastructure :: Advanced Micro Devices, Inc. (AMD) # AMD and Meta Advance Strategic Partnership to Power Meta’s Superintelligence Infrastructure October 27, 2026 9:20 am EDT Download as PDF News Highlights - AMD and Meta collaborate across CPUs, GPUs, networking, systems and software to power Meta services and AI infrastructure - AMD Helios rackscale solutions will power Meta’s leading frontier models and services - AMD technology is the compute engine of choice for Muse and AMD technologies provide Day-0 support for leading Meta models SANTA CLARA, Calif., Oct. 27, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- AMD (NASDAQ: AMD) today highlighted its deep strategic partnership with Meta, announcing AMD Helios™ rackscale solutions are running at Meta, AMD EPYC™ processors power Meta’s Muse AI agent, and AMD technologies provide Day-0 support for Meta models including Muse Spark Open and Muse Glimmer. This builds on years of co-design and collaboration between the two companies across AMD EPYC™ processors, AMD Instinct™ GPUs, AMD Pensando™ networking and AMD ROCm™ AI infrastructure.

sources.summary: Summary: - AMD announced on September 26, 2026 that it agreed to acquire all equity interests in World Labs Technologies, Inc. for about $8.2 billion, to be paid in AMD common stock. - The exact number of AMD shares to be issued will be determined using the 10-day VWAP ending just before closing, and is currently unknown. - The issuance will rely on exemptions from registration under Section 4(a)(2) and/or Rule 506 of Regulation D, and is not a public offering (no public solicitation). Context note: The filing indicates a stock-based acquisition of World Labs, with pricing and closing mechanics to be finalized, and no immediate public market implications beyond standard SEC disclosures.

Item 3.02 Unregistered Sales of Equity Securities On September 26, 2026, Advanced Micro Devices, Inc. (the “Company”) entered into an Agreement and Plan of Merger (the “Merger Agreement”) to acquire all of the equity interests in World Labs Technologies, Inc. (“World Labs”) (the “Acquisition”) for a total purchase price of approximately $8.2 billion to be paid in shares of the Company’s common stock, par value $0.01 per share (“Common Stock”), to stockholders of World Labs, subject to customary adjustments. At this time, the number of shares to be issued in connection with the Acquisition is not known and will be calculated based on the daily volume-weighted average price of a share of Common Stock on the Nasdaq Global Select Market over the ten (10) consecutive trading-day period ending on and including the second trading day immediately preceding the closing date of the Acquisition.
